ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a fixed smooth inclined plane on a horizontal surface with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$. To keep a positively charged small ball with mass $m$ and charge $q$ stationary on the inclined plane, different electric fields can be applied. The gravitational acceleration is $g$.

1. If the direction of the field strength is vertically upward, find the magnitude of the field strength $E_1$.
2. If the direction of the field strength is horizontally to the left, find the magnitude of the field strength $E_2$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a fixed smooth inclined plane on a horizontal surface with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$. To keep a positively charged small ball with mass $m$ and charge $q$ stationary on the inclined plane, different electric fields can be applied. The gravitational acceleration is $g$. 1. If the direction of the field strength is vertically upward, find the magnitude of the field strength $E_1$. 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a smooth inclined plane fixed on a horizontal surface, higher on the left and lower on the right, with an inclination angle of 45° relative to the horizontal surface; a small ball is at rest on the inclined plane. Since the inclined plane is smooth, along the direction of the inclined plane it is only necessary to balance the components of gravity and the electric field force; the supporting force is perpendicular to the inclined plane and does not participate in the balance along the inclined plane. Reasoning: Take upward along the inclined plane as the positive direction. The small ball is positively charged, so the direction of the electric field force is the same as the direction of the electric field. 1. When the electric field is vertically upward, the magnitude of the electric field force is qE1, and its component upward along the inclined plane is qE1 sin45°; the component of gravity mg downward along the inclined plane is mg sin45°. The condition for rest is qE1 sin45° = mg sin45°, so E1 = mg/q. 2. When the electric field is horizontally to the left, the magnitude of the electric field force is qE2, directed horizontally to the left, and in the figure it has a component upward along the inclined plane qE2 cos45°; the component of gravity along the inclined plane downward is mg sin45°. The condition for rest is qE2 cos45° = mg sin45°. Since sin45°=cos45°, E2 = mg/q.
